privacy_policy_intro: OpenAthlete is a training platform for endurance athletes and their coaches: planning, sync with your watch and training analysis. Some features use artificial intelligence, only after you allow it. This Privacy Policy explains what data we collect, how we use it, and your rights.
privacy_policy_data_we_collect_list_2: Profile information (sport preferences, roles, timezone, language).
privacy_policy_data_we_collect_list_3: Training and activity data (planned sessions, completed activities, metrics, notes).
privacy_policy_data_we_collect_list_4: Device and connector data from integrated providers such as Garmin or Strava (activity files, GPS, heart rate, power, cadence, sleep, steps, body composition, wellness metrics), when you connect those services.
privacy_policy_data_we_collect_list_5: Health-related data that you choose to share (e.g., heart rate, HRV, VO₂max, injuries), which we treat as sensitive information.
privacy_policy_data_we_collect_list_7: AI interaction data (prompts and model outputs) to provide AI-assisted features. We do not use your data to train AI models.
privacy_policy_data_we_collect_list_8: Usage, diagnostics, and device information (logs, browser, IP, app performance) to maintain security and reliability.
privacy_policy_how_we_use_list_1: Provide the core service, including planning, tracking, and collaboration between coaches and athletes.
privacy_policy_how_we_use_list_2: With your consent, run AI features on your data: generating or editing a session from a sentence, a short summary of each activity, questions after an activity and the effort and pain notes taken from your answers, and load estimates for planned sessions. The AI suggests; it does not diagnose or predict injuries.
privacy_policy_how_we_use_list_3: Sync with connected providers (e.g., Garmin) to import activities and export workouts with your authorization.
privacy_policy_how_we_use_list_4: Communicate with you (service messages, notifications) and provide support.
privacy_policy_how_we_use_list_5: Maintain security, prevent abuse, and debug issues.
privacy_policy_how_we_use_list_6: Product improvement using aggregated usage statistics, and, only if you accept, product analytics and masked session recordings.
privacy_policy_legal_basis_list_1: Consent: for connecting third-party providers, processing sensitive health data, sending your data to AI providers, product analytics and session recordings, and receiving certain communications.
privacy_policy_legal_basis_list_2: Contract: to deliver the service you request and manage your account.
privacy_policy_legal_basis_list_3: Legitimate interests: to secure our services, prevent misuse, and improve features in a way that does not override your rights.
privacy_policy_sharing_list_1: Service providers acting on our behalf under data processing agreements, listed below.
privacy_policy_sharing_list_2: Integrations you choose to connect (e.g., Garmin, Strava). We share or receive data strictly to provide the requested functionality.
privacy_policy_sharing_list_3: Coach–athlete collaboration: data you explicitly share within a space (e.g., plans, comments, metrics) is visible to invited members according to your settings.
privacy_policy_sharing_list_4: Legal compliance or to protect rights, safety, and security when required by law or to prevent fraud or abuse.
privacy_policy_data_retention_content: We keep personal data only as long as necessary to provide the service, comply with legal obligations, resolve disputes, and enforce agreements. You may request deletion; some records may be retained as required by law or for legitimate business purposes.
privacy_policy_security_content: We apply administrative, technical, and organizational measures to protect personal data, including encryption in transit, access controls, and monitoring. No system is 100% secure; we continuously improve our safeguards.
privacy_policy_international_transfers_c: If data is transferred internationally, we rely on lawful mechanisms (e.g., Standard Contractual Clauses) and implement appropriate safeguards.
privacy_policy_your_rights_list_1: Access, correction, deletion, and portability of your data: download all of it from Settings > Profile > Download my data, and delete your account from the same page.
privacy_policy_your_rights_list_2: Restriction or objection to certain processing, including withdrawals of consent at any time.
privacy_policy_your_rights_list_3: Right to lodge a complaint with a data protection authority.
privacy_policy_children_content: OpenAthlete is not intended for children under 16. We do not knowingly collect data from children. If you believe a child has provided personal data, contact us and we will take appropriate action.
privacy_policy_changes_content: We may update this policy to reflect changes in our practices or legal requirements. We will post updates with a new effective date.
privacy_policy_processors_list_1: OVHcloud (France): servers and database of the service.
privacy_policy_processors_list_2: Vercel (United States): delivery of the website and web application (technical logs such as IP addresses).
privacy_policy_processors_list_3: PostHog (European Union data region): error reports and server logs, which name no user.
privacy_policy_processors_list_4: PostHog and Contentsquare: product analytics and masked session recordings, only if you accept them.
privacy_policy_processors_list_5: Brevo (France): transactional emails such as password resets and invitations.
privacy_policy_processors_list_7: Google Firebase: sign-in with Google and push notifications on mobile.
privacy_policy_processors_list_8: AI providers: nothing is sent to them until you allow it, in the app (Settings > AI shows what is sent and to whom, and lets you withdraw it). With your own API key, the provider you choose processes the data each AI feature needs, under your agreement with it. With AI included in your plan, OpenAI and Google process it on our behalf, and OpenAI transcribes the voice notes you record.
privacy_policy_cookies_content: The app stores what it needs to work (your login session and preferences) on your device. Product analytics and session recordings only start after you accept them in the consent banner, and you can change your choice at any time in Settings > Profile. Refusing does not limit any feature. The website measures visits with PostHog and never records sessions. Until you accept in its banner, it stores nothing on your device: PostHog counts visitors with a hash of the IP address and browser, computed on its servers and renewed every day, which cannot follow you from one day to the next. You can change your choice at the bottom of any page. Once accepted, the PostHog cookie is shared between openathlete.org and app.openathlete.org, so that a visit to the website followed by a sign-up counts as one visitor. Links from the website to the app carry where your visit started, whether you accept or not: the campaign parameters (utm) of the link that brought you, the site that sent you (its name only), the first page you saw and the page of the link you followed. Before you accept, they are kept in the open page only, never on your device. When you sign up, the app records them with your account, along with your answer to “How did you hear about OpenAthlete?”, so we learn which channels bring new users (legitimate interest). They are part of your data export and deleted with your account.
privacy_policy_self_hosting_content: OpenAthlete is open source and can be self-hosted. On an instance you do not run on openathlete.org, its operator is responsible for your data; none of it is sent to OpenAthlete.
privacy_policy_contact_content: If you have questions or requests regarding privacy, contact us at contact@openathlete.org.

home_seo_title: OpenAthlete: the free, open-source TrainingPeaks alternative
home_seo_description: Plan your season, send structured workouts to Garmin, COROS or Suunto, track fitness and fatigue, coach your athletes. Free, open source, hosted in Europe.
home_hero_lead: Plan your season, send structured workouts to your watch, follow fitness and fatigue, coach your athletes. Free on our servers, free on yours.
home_hero_shot_alt: OpenAthlete training calendar with planned and completed sessions
home_logos_title: Works with the watch you already wear
home_paths_athlete_body: Every feature is free: calendar, workout builder, watch sync, analysis, records, training load. Bring your own AI key if you want it.
home_paths_coach_body: Five athletes free, then €50 a year for as many as you like. Your athletes never pay to get your sessions on their watch.
home_tour_title: From the plan to the watch to the analysis.
home_tour_lead: The loop every endurance athlete runs each week, in one place, with nothing locked behind a paywall.
home_tour_plan_title: A calendar that thinks in seasons, weeks and sessions
home_tour_plan_body: Lay out your training blocks and A, B and C races on a season view, then fill the weeks. Copy a week, shift it, undo it. Mark an illness or a trip and the sessions it covers are moved for you.
home_tour_plan_point_2: Copy, paste and shift whole weeks
home_tour_plan_point_3: Calendar feed for Google, Apple or Outlook
home_tour_build_title: Structured workouts that land on your wrist
home_tour_build_body: Warm-up, 5 × 4 minutes at threshold, cool-down. Set targets in pace, power, heart rate or % of your zones, and the session appears on your Garmin, COROS or Suunto the next time it syncs.
home_tour_build_point_3: Describe a session in words, AI writes the steps
home_tour_analyse_title: Every activity graded against what was planned
home_tour_analyse_body: Intervals and climbs are detected on their own. You see each step next to its target, time in zones, aerobic decoupling, and pace adjusted for the gradient and the weather on the day.
home_tour_analyse_point_3: Fix heart-rate spikes, undo any time
home_tour_records_title: Records and capacities that update themselves
home_tour_records_body: Best efforts by distance and duration, year against year. Critical speed and critical power estimated from what you actually ran and rode, with race-time ranges you can trust a little more than a calculator.
home_tour_coach_title: See who needs you this morning
home_tour_coach_body: Compliance, volume and form for each athlete on one screen. Alerts when someone reports pain, goes quiet, or leaves a message unread. Comment on a session, chat one to one or with a group.
home_tour_coach_point_1: Plan for many athletes at once
home_load_title: Know when to push, and when to back off.
home_load_body: Fitness, fatigue and form are computed from heart rate or perceived effort, then projected over the sessions you have planned. You see the taper working before race day, not after.
home_load_open: No black box: the formulas are in the source code, and every metric in the app says what it measures and where it stops being reliable.
home_ai_title: Use the AI you already pay for.
home_ai_body: Paste a key from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral or OpenRouter and pick the model for each task. No key? Supporter includes a monthly allowance on ours. Either way, nothing runs until you say yes.
home_ai_feature_1_body: "Hilly 90-minute run with 3 × 8' at threshold" becomes a structured workout with your zones.
home_ai_feature_2_body: A short summary after each upload, and three questions on how it felt. Your answers become effort and pain notes your coach sees.
home_ai_feature_3_title: Talk to your training from Claude or ChatGPT
home_ai_feature_3_body: Connect OpenAthlete as an MCP server. Ask about last month, or have it plan your next block straight into your calendar.
home_ai_prompt: My calf is tight after Sunday's long run. Adjust this week, keep Thursday's session if you can.
home_ai_reply: Moved Tuesday's hills to Wednesday as an easy 45' run, kept Thursday's 5 × 4' but on flat ground, and swapped Saturday's trail for a ride. 3 sessions updated.
home_cost_title: Coaching software shouldn't cost more than your race entry.
home_cost_lead: Move the slider to your roster size. Yearly list prices, checked on the vendors' pricing pages.
home_os_title: The training platform nobody can buy out from under you.
home_os_body: Today's Plan shut down in March 2024 and its coaches had to pack up and move. TrainingPeaks now belongs to a watch maker. OpenAthlete's code is public under AGPL-3.0: if we ever stopped, you could run it yourself the next day, with all your history.
home_os_point_1: Self-host with one Docker Compose file
home_os_point_2: Full JSON export, account deletion that really deletes
home_os_point_3: A self-hosted instance sends us nothing. An automated test checks it on every change.
home_pricing_title: Free for everyone. €5 a month if you want to help.
home_pricing_lead: Supporter pays for the servers and the AI, and lets coaches go past five athletes. It is how a project with no investors stays independent.
home_mobile_title: The Android app is out. iPhone is next
home_mobile_body: Install OpenAthlete from Google Play. The iPhone app is in testing; until it reaches the App Store, add OpenAthlete to your home screen: it is built for phones.
home_faq_1_a: Yes. Every feature works on a free account: planning, watch sync, analysis, training load, coaching up to five athletes, and AI with your own key. Supporter (€5 a month or €50 a year) adds AI on our keys and unlimited coached athletes.
home_faq_2_q: Which watches and apps does it work with?
home_faq_2_a: Activities come in from Garmin, COROS, Suunto, Polar and Strava, or as FIT, GPX and TCX files. Planned workouts are sent to Garmin, COROS and Suunto watches; sending them to Polar isn't possible yet.
home_faq_3_q: Can I bring my history from TrainingPeaks or Strava?
home_faq_3_a: Connect Strava or your watch account and your past activities are imported (how far back depends on each brand). You can also upload FIT, GPX and TCX files in bulk, for example an export from another platform.
home_faq_4_q: Do I need to pay for the AI?
home_faq_4_a: No. Add your own key from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, OpenRouter or another provider and the AI features work on a free account. Supporter includes a monthly allowance on our keys if you'd rather not manage one. The AI only runs after you allow it, and you can take that back.
home_faq_5_q: Who is behind OpenAthlete, and will it last?
home_faq_5_a: An independent developer in Grenoble, France, with contributors on GitHub and no investors. Supporters pay for the servers. Because the code is open source, the platform doesn't depend on us: you can export everything at any time, or run your own copy.
home_faq_6_a: Yes. The Android app is on Google Play. The native iPhone app is in testing and will reach the App Store soon; until then, the web app is designed for phones and can be added to your home screen.
home_faq_7_a: On the hosted service, the API and the database run on OVH servers in France; the web app itself is served by Vercel. If you self-host, your data never leaves your own server.
home_final_title: Your next block starts on Monday.
home_final_body: Create an account, connect your watch, and your history is there before your coffee is cold.

features_cal_seo_title: Training calendar for runners, cyclists and triathletes
features_cal_seo_description: Plan weeks and seasons on a drag-and-drop calendar: races, periods, planned vs completed sessions, synced from your watch. Free on OpenAthlete.
features_cal_title: A training calendar built for endurance sports
features_cal_lead: Races, training blocks, planned sessions and what you actually did, on one calendar. Drag a session to Thursday, copy last week, log two days of flu: the plan follows.
features_cal_proof_3: Free, on our servers or yours
features_cal_season_body: Press S and the calendar folds into a season: 6 or 12 months, one row per week. Drag across weeks to draw a block, give it a phase, drop your races on it with an A, B or C priority. Each week shows the duration and load done and planned, with the form you are heading for.
features_cal_season_point_1: Phases: base, specific, taper, recovery, competition
features_cal_season_point_2: Weekly load against a recommended range
features_cal_season_point_3: Form projected over the sessions still to do
features_cal_strip_load: Bars: weekly load (TRIMP), every fourth week lighter
features_cal_match_body: When your run arrives from the watch, it lands on the session planned that day. If you swapped days, drag the activity onto the right session, or pick one of up to three suggestions. A coloured strip then tells you how close you were to the plan, on duration or distance.
features_cal_match_point_1: Wellness on each day: sleep, HRV, resting HR, Hooper index
features_cal_match_point_2: Week totals: duration, distance, elevation, load
features_cal_match_point_3: Optional rule: a session only counts with an RPE or a comment
features_cal_tools_lead: The boring part of planning, done in a few clicks. Every bulk action can be undone.
features_cal_tool_1_body: Last week worked. Paste it into the next one and change the long run.
features_cal_tool_2_title: Shift by a day or a week
features_cal_tool_2_body: A work trip on Monday: push the rest of the week back by one day.
features_cal_tool_3_body: Ctrl or Cmd + Z, or the button in the toast. The whole week comes back.
features_cal_tool_4_body: Every 1 to 4 weeks, up to 90 days ahead. Edit this one or this one and the following.
features_cal_tool_5_body: Open the library on the side, drop a saved workout on any day.
features_cal_tool_6_title: Drop a file on a day
features_cal_tool_6_body: A FIT, GPX or TCX from an old watch goes straight onto the right date.
features_cal_tool_7_body: Jump to an activity, an athlete or a page from anywhere.
features_cal_tool_8_body: Compact or comfortable, and you choose what each card shows. It follows your account to every device.
features_cal_periods_body: Drag across the days you will not train and pick Illness, Injury or Travel. The period is drawn hatched on the calendar. If it covers sessions still to do, OpenAthlete asks what to do with them: move them after the period, or delete them.
features_cal_periods_note: From Claude or ChatGPT, "I've had a fever since yesterday" does the same through the MCP server, then adapts the next sessions.
features_cal_dialog_body: 2 sessions are planned during this period.
features_cal_coach_title: Shared with your coach in real time
features_cal_coach_body: Your coach plans on the same calendar you train from. Changes show up live on both screens, without a refresh. Each session and activity has its own comment thread, and unread comments are flagged on the calendar.
features_cal_coach_point_1: Several coaches per athlete if you need them
features_cal_coach_point_2: Coaches select sessions and move, copy or delete them in bulk
features_cal_feed_title: Your sessions in Google, Apple or Outlook Calendar
features_cal_feed_body: Subscribe to a private iCal link and your planned sessions, races and notes appear in the calendar you already use for work, as all-day events with the full workout in the description. The link is secret; generate a new one and the old one stops working.
features_cal_faq_1_a: Running, trail, road and gravel cycling, mountain biking, swimming, triathlon and duathlon, rowing, Nordic skiing, strength and about fifty other sport types. A week can mix them, and the totals are kept per sport.
features_cal_faq_2_q: Does my watch activity attach to the planned session by itself?
features_cal_faq_2_a: Yes, when it happens on the same day as a planned session. If you trained on another day, drag the activity onto the session or choose among up to three suggestions. You can unlink it too.
features_cal_faq_3_q: Can my coach edit my calendar?
features_cal_faq_3_a: Yes. A coach you have accepted plans, moves and comments on your calendar, and you see the changes live. You can have more than one coach.
features_cal_faq_4_q: Can I see my sessions in Google Calendar?
features_cal_faq_4_a: Yes, through the iCal feed in your settings. It is one-way: Google, Apple or Outlook Calendar show your sessions, races and notes; edits are made in OpenAthlete.
features_cal_faq_5_a: Nothing. Every feature is free on OpenAthlete Cloud and on a self-hosted instance. The €5 Supporter plan only adds AI on our keys and unlimited coached athletes.
features_cal_faq_6_q: Does it work on a phone?
features_cal_faq_6_a: Yes. On a phone the week view stacks the days and opens on a Today screen. Install the Android app from Google Play, or the web app on your home screen; the iPhone app is in testing.
features_cal_final_title: Put next week on the calendar
features_cal_final_body: Connect your watch, drag in a few sessions, and see how Sunday's form looks before you get there.

connect_sync_title: What comes in, what goes out
connect_sync_lead: Each brand decides what its API shares. Here is exactly what the {provider} connection does today.
connect_step_1_body: In the web app or the installed app. New accounts see the same list during onboarding.
connect_limits_lead: Better to read them here than to find out on race week.
connect_limit_selfhost: On a self-hosted instance, {provider} only appears if the admin has registered the instance with {provider}'s developer program. COROS, file upload and the Activity Import API work without that.
connect_garmin_lead: Plan Tuesday's 5 × 4' at threshold in OpenAthlete and it shows up on your Garmin calendar, then on the watch. The run comes back after the sync, with laps, heart rate and power, right next to the plan.
connect_garmin_tagline: Workouts to the watch. Activities, sleep and HRV back.
connect_garmin_note_activities: Garmin pushes each new activity once your watch has synced, FIT file included: laps, heart rate, power, cadence.
connect_garmin_note_history: The last 30 days: that is what Garmin hands over per request. Upload older FIT files if you want them.
connect_garmin_note_metrics: Opt-in: sleep stages and score, HRV, resting heart rate, stress, Body Battery, steps, VO2max, body composition and more.
connect_garmin_note_workouts: Structured sessions go to your Garmin Connect calendar and reach the watch at its next sync. Move or edit one and the Garmin copy follows. Running, cycling, pool swimming, strength, cardio, yoga and pilates.
connect_garmin_step_2: Click Connect next to Garmin. Garmin opens its sign-in page: log in and accept the permissions it lists.
connect_garmin_step_3: Import sessions and Export workouts are on by default. Turn on Import metrics if you want sleep, HRV and Body Battery in OpenAthlete.
connect_garmin_step_4: Press Import all activities to bring in the last 30 days. For older runs, drop their FIT files on the calendar.
connect_garmin_limit_1: History import stops at 30 days. Older activities come in as FIT files; one that starts at the same time as an activity already there is refused, so you can't create doubles.
connect_garmin_limit_2: If you refuse activity sharing on Garmin's consent page, Garmin also refuses the history import. Reconnect and leave it allowed.
connect_garmin_limit_3: A session with only a duration and no steps sends nothing to the watch: there is nothing for it to guide.
connect_garmin_faq_1_a: Activities come from any device that syncs with Garmin Connect. Planned workouts need a device that can follow structured workouts from the Garmin Connect calendar; your model's manual will tell you.
connect_garmin_faq_2_q: My workout isn't on my watch. What do I check?
connect_garmin_faq_2_a: Three things: Export workouts is on in Settings > Connectors, the session has structured steps, and the watch has synced with Garmin Connect since you planned it.
connect_garmin_faq_3_q: My coach plans my sessions. Do they reach my Garmin?
connect_garmin_faq_3_a: Yes. Sessions your coach puts on your calendar go out through your own Garmin connection, like the ones you plan yourself. Your coach doesn't need a Garmin account.
connect_garmin_faq_4_a: Settings > Connectors, then Disconnect. OpenAthlete stops receiving Garmin data. Deleting your OpenAthlete account also removes the connection on Garmin's side.
connect_garmin_final_title: Your next interval session, already on your Garmin.
connect_garmin_final_body: Create a free account, connect Garmin, plan a session, sync the watch.
connect_coros_lead: Run, trail and bike sessions planned in OpenAthlete go to your COROS watch. Activities, sleep and HRV come back, history included. The connector is brand new: if something looks off, tell us on Discord.
connect_coros_tagline: Run, trail and bike workouts out. Activities, history and HRV in.
connect_coros_note_activities: COROS has no instant notifications, so OpenAthlete checks for new activities about every 30 minutes.
connect_coros_note_history: Your whole history, but COROS serves 50 activity files a day, so a few years take several days to arrive.
connect_coros_note_metrics: Opt-in: HRV, resting heart rate, sleep, naps and VO2max.
connect_coros_note_workouts: Running, trail running and cycling sessions. Swims and strength sessions aren't sent.
connect_coros_step_2: Click Connect next to COROS and pick the region where you created your account: Europe, United States and other regions, or Mainland China. Then sign in to COROS.
connect_coros_step_3: Import sessions and Export workouts are on by default. Turn on Import metrics for HRV, sleep and resting heart rate.
connect_coros_step_4: Press Import all activities, then forget about it. At 50 files a day, the history fills in over the following days.
connect_coros_limit_1: COROS can't delete a planned session. One you move or remove in OpenAthlete stays on the COROS calendar, marked as cancelled, until you delete it in the COROS app.
connect_coros_limit_2: A new activity can take up to about 30 minutes to show up.
connect_coros_limit_3: The connector went live in November 2026. It works, but it hasn't met every watch and every edge case yet.
connect_coros_faq_1_q: Does COROS work on a self-hosted instance?
connect_coros_faq_1_a: Yes, with no developer account to request: each connection registers itself with COROS. It is the one watch brand a self-hosted instance gets out of the box.
connect_coros_faq_2_q: Why does my history take days?
connect_coros_faq_2_a: COROS lets an app download 50 activity files a day. OpenAthlete takes them as they come, newest first. Nothing to do on your side.
connect_coros_faq_3_a: The one where you created your COROS account: COROS keeps each account on one regional server. Picked the wrong one? Disconnect and connect again with the other.
connect_coros_faq_4_q: Can my coach send sessions to my COROS?
connect_coros_faq_4_a: Yes. Run, trail and bike sessions your coach plans on your calendar go out through your COROS connection. Your coach can use any watch, or none.
connect_coros_final_title: Real structured sessions on your COROS.
connect_coros_final_body: Create a free account, connect COROS, plan your next threshold run.
connect_suunto_lead: Structured sessions go to your Suunto watch as guides. Every activity comes back with its laps, and your sleep and HRV can follow.
connect_suunto_tagline: Workouts as Suunto guides. Activities, sleep and HRV back.
connect_suunto_note_activities: Suunto notifies OpenAthlete when an activity reaches your Suunto account, FIT file and laps included.
connect_suunto_note_history: The last 30 days. Upload older FIT files if you want to go further back.
connect_suunto_note_metrics: Opt-in: sleep stages and score, HRV, daily heart rate, steps, calories, SpO2, naps and resources.
connect_suunto_note_workouts: Running, trail running, cycling and swimming sessions, sent as guides you follow from the watch.
connect_suunto_step_2: Click Connect next to Suunto, sign in with your Suunto account and allow access.
connect_suunto_step_3: Import sessions and Export workouts are on by default. Turn on Import metrics for sleep, HRV and daily heart rate.
connect_suunto_step_4: Press Import all activities to bring in the last 30 days. Older sessions come in as FIT files dropped on the calendar.
connect_suunto_limit_1: Workouts out cover running, trail running, cycling and swimming. Strength sessions stay in OpenAthlete.
connect_suunto_limit_2: History import stops at 30 days. A FIT file that starts at the same time as an activity already there is refused, so older uploads won't create doubles.
connect_suunto_limit_3: A session with only a duration and no steps sends nothing: a guide needs steps.
connect_suunto_faq_1_q: Where do I find the workout on my Suunto?
connect_suunto_faq_1_a: It arrives as a guide in your Suunto account. Pick that guide when you start the exercise on the watch, like any other Suunto guide.
connect_suunto_faq_2_q: My session didn't reach the watch. What do I check?
connect_suunto_faq_2_a: That Export workouts is on in Settings > Connectors, that the session has structured steps and a supported sport, and that the watch has synced with the Suunto app since.
connect_suunto_faq_3_q: My coach plans my sessions. Do they reach my Suunto?
connect_suunto_faq_3_a: Yes, through your own Suunto connection, exactly like the sessions you plan yourself.
connect_suunto_faq_4_a: Settings > Connectors, then Disconnect. Deleting your OpenAthlete account also removes the connection on Suunto's side.
connect_suunto_final_title: Plan here, follow the guide on your Suunto.
connect_suunto_final_body: Create a free account, connect Suunto, send your first guide.
connect_polar_lead: Activities recorded on your Polar come into OpenAthlete with heart rate, laps and route, plus sleep and nightly HRV if you turn them on. Workouts can't go the other way: Polar's API doesn't accept them.
connect_polar_tagline: Activities, sleep and nightly HRV in. No workouts out.
connect_polar_note_activities: Polar notifies OpenAthlete when an activity reaches Polar Flow, and an hourly check catches anything missed.
connect_polar_note_history: Polar only shares what reaches Flow after you connect, for 30 days. Older sessions come in as files.
connect_polar_note_metrics: Opt-in: daily activity, sleep, nightly HRV, weight, VO2max, max and resting heart rate.
connect_polar_note_workouts: Polar's API is read-only. Follow the session from the OpenAthlete app on your phone instead.
connect_polar_step_2: Click Connect next to Polar, sign in to Polar Flow and allow access.
connect_polar_step_3: Import sessions is on by default. Turn on Import metrics for sleep, nightly HRV and weight.
connect_polar_step_4: Polar has no history button. Download older sessions from Polar Flow and drop the files on the OpenAthlete calendar.
connect_polar_limit_1: No workouts on Polar watches: Polar's API only lets apps read.
connect_polar_limit_2: No history import: only activities that reach Flow after you connect, within 30 days.
connect_polar_limit_3: Sleep and HRV stay off until you turn on Import metrics.
connect_polar_faq_1_q: Can OpenAthlete send workouts to my Polar watch?
connect_polar_faq_1_a: No. Polar's API lets apps read data, not write it. If structured sessions on the wrist matter most to you, Garmin, Suunto and COROS are the brands OpenAthlete can send to.
connect_polar_faq_2_q: Can I bring in my old Polar sessions?
connect_polar_faq_2_a: Yes, as files. Download them from Polar Flow and upload them in OpenAthlete, several at once. A session that starts at the same time as one already there is refused, so overlaps are safe.
connect_polar_faq_3_a: Only if you turn on Import metrics. It is off by default, because not everyone wants their nights on a coach's screen.
connect_polar_faq_4_a: Settings > Connectors, then Disconnect. Deleting your OpenAthlete account also removes the connection on Polar's side.
connect_polar_final_title: Your Polar data, next to your plan.
connect_polar_final_body: Create a free account, connect Polar Flow, and your next session lands on the calendar.
connect_strava_lead: Keep Strava for kudos and segments. OpenAthlete reads a copy of every activity, back to your first upload, and turns it into training load, records and analysis.
connect_strava_tagline: Activities and full history in. Nothing sent back.
connect_strava_note_activities: Strava notifies OpenAthlete of each new activity, which arrives with its full data streams.
connect_strava_note_history: Your whole Strava history, from the first upload.
connect_strava_note_metrics: Strava doesn't share sleep or HRV. Connect your watch brand directly for those.
connect_strava_note_workouts: Strava doesn't take planned workouts. Connect Garmin, Suunto or COROS to get sessions on your watch.
connect_strava_step_2: Click Connect next to Strava, sign in to Strava and authorize OpenAthlete.
connect_strava_step_3: Import sessions is on by default. With Strava, that is the only switch.
connect_strava_step_4: Press Import all activities. A long history arrives in the background over the next minutes; you can keep using the app.
connect_strava_limit_1: Activities only: no planned workouts out, no sleep or HRV in.
connect_strava_limit_2: OpenAthlete only asks for read access. It never posts, comments or gives kudos on your behalf.
connect_strava_limit_3: If your watch is a Garmin, Suunto, COROS or Polar, connecting it directly also brings wellness data and, except for Polar, workouts on the watch.
connect_strava_faq_1_q: Will OpenAthlete post anything to my Strava?
connect_strava_faq_1_a: No. The connection only reads your activities. Nothing is posted, changed or deleted on Strava.
connect_strava_faq_2_q: Do my private activities come in too?
connect_strava_faq_2_a: Yes. OpenAthlete asks for access to all your activities, private ones included, so your training load isn't missing the runs you keep to yourself. They stay private in OpenAthlete too: only you and your coaches see them.
connect_strava_faq_3_q: Can I send my planned sessions to Strava?
connect_strava_faq_3_a: No: Strava has nowhere to put them. To follow a structured session on the wrist, connect Garmin, Suunto or COROS.
connect_strava_faq_4_a: Settings > Connectors, then Disconnect. You can also revoke access from your Strava settings.
connect_strava_final_title: Keep the kudos. Add a training plan.
connect_strava_final_body: Create a free account, connect Strava, and see years of runs turned into fitness and fatigue.
connect_hub_seo_title: Garmin, COROS, Suunto, Polar and Strava sync | OpenAthlete
connect_hub_seo_description: What syncs from Garmin, COROS, Suunto, Polar and Strava, what goes back to the watch, plus FIT/GPX/TCX upload, an import API and a calendar feed.
connect_hub_lead: Activities come in from Garmin, COROS, Suunto, Polar and Strava. Planned workouts go out to Garmin, Suunto and COROS. Every connection is free.
connect_hub_matrix_lead: The limits come from each brand's API, not from your plan. Polar's API is read-only, Garmin and Suunto hand over 30 days of history, COROS takes its time.
connect_hub_other_title: Files, an API and a calendar feed
connect_hub_other_lead: For the watch that isn't on the list, the app you built yourself, and the family calendar.
connect_hub_files_body: Drop files on a calendar day or upload several at once, up to 20 MB each. FIT and TCX keep their laps. A file that starts at the same time as an activity already there is refused, so uploading twice is harmless.
connect_hub_files_note: Multisport FIT files aren't supported yet.
connect_hub_api_body: Another app, such as a self-hosted activity tracker, can push FIT, GPX and TCX files to your calendar. It signs in with OAuth 2.1 and gets one scope, activities:import: it can send files, not read anything.
connect_hub_ical_body: Subscribe from Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or any app that reads iCal. Planned sessions, races and notes show up as all-day events with their full details. The link is secret, and you can regenerate it.
connect_hub_selfhost_title: On your own server, COROS works out of the box.
connect_hub_selfhost_body: Garmin, Suunto, Polar and Strava only open their APIs to registered developers, so a self-hosted instance offers them only if its admin has signed up with each. COROS needs nothing: every connection registers itself. File upload and the Activity Import API work everywhere.
connect_hub_faq_1_q: Do I have to pay to connect my watch?
connect_hub_faq_1_a: No. Every connection works on the free plan and on self-hosted instances. Supporter adds AI on our keys and unlimited coached athletes, nothing else.
connect_hub_faq_2_q: Can I connect more than one service?
connect_hub_faq_2_a: Yes. Each one has its own switches for activities, workouts and metrics in Settings > Connectors. If your watch brand has its own connection, prefer it to Strava: you also get wellness data, and workouts on the watch with Garmin, Suunto and COROS.
connect_hub_faq_3_q: Why can't OpenAthlete send workouts to Polar or Strava?
connect_hub_faq_3_a: Their APIs don't take planned workouts: Polar's is read-only, and Strava has no workout feature to send to. Garmin, Suunto and COROS do accept them.
connect_hub_faq_4_q: What about Wahoo, Zwift or Apple Health?
connect_hub_faq_4_a: Not supported today. If your device or app exports FIT, GPX or TCX files, upload them, or have an app push them through the Activity Import API.
connect_hub_faq_5_q: Do my athletes need the same watch brand?
connect_hub_faq_5_a: No. Each athlete connects their own account. You plan on their calendar, and the session goes out through whatever they connected: a Garmin for one, a COROS for another. Polar and Strava users follow it from the app.
connect_hub_final_title: Plan here. Train with the watch you have.
connect_hub_final_body: Create a free account, then pick your service in Settings > Connectors.
features_wb_seo_title: Workout builder: send workouts to Garmin, COROS and Suunto
features_wb_seo_description: Build structured intervals with pace, heart rate, power or % VMA targets and send them to Garmin, COROS or Suunto. Your watch guides every rep.
features_wb_title: Build a workout once, run it on your watch
features_wb_lead: Warm-up, 5 × 4' at threshold with 2' jog, cool-down. Write it with your own zones, save it to your library, put it on Tuesday. Your Garmin, Suunto or COROS beeps you through every rep.
features_wb_targets_body: Each step gets a duration and one or more targets. Use a fixed value, a range, one of your zones, or a percentage of a reference: VMA, FTP, critical power, maximum heart rate or heart rate reserve.
features_wb_targets_example: 80% of VMA with a VMA of 18 km/h is 14.4 km/h, so 4:10 per km. The percentage is converted with your latest value when the workout is sent to the watch.
features_wb_duration_4: HR below or above a value
features_wb_send_title: Sent to Garmin, Suunto and COROS automatically
features_wb_send_body: Turn on workout export for your connected watch once. From then on, every structured session you or your coach plans goes to the watch for its date, and edits follow. Two services in the list do not take workouts at all, and we would rather say so here than in a support ticket.
features_wb_send_garmin: Through the Garmin Training API, onto your Garmin Connect calendar and the watch. Running, cycling, pool swimming, strength, cardio, yoga, pilates.
features_wb_send_suunto: As Suunto guides, for running, trail, cycling and swimming.
features_wb_send_coros: Running, trail running and cycling. The connector is new. COROS cannot delete a planned workout, so a deleted session leaves a "removed" placeholder.
features_wb_send_polar: Polar's API does not accept planned workouts. Activities and wellness data come in; nothing goes out.
features_wb_send_strava: Strava has no planned workouts. It is a source of activities only.
features_wb_library_title: A workout library you build once
features_wb_library_body: Save any session as a template and file it in coloured folders, nested as deep as you like. Open the library next to the calendar and drag a template onto a day. Coaches drop their own templates onto any athlete's calendar.
features_wb_ai_title: Type the session, get the steps
features_wb_ai_body: If you have an AI key connected (or Supporter), write the session the way you would text it to a friend. The AI fills in the steps with your zones. You check it and edit it like any other workout.
features_wb_ai_prompt: 15' easy, 3 × 10' at threshold with 2' jog, 10' cool-down
features_wb_ai_link: What the AI does, and does not do
features_wb_sport_run_body: Pace per km, % VMA, heart rate, running power.
features_wb_sport_swim_body: Pace per 100 m, steps by distance, rest intervals.
features_wb_sport_strength_body: Reps and weight per step, notes for each exercise.
features_wb_trouble_title: My workout isn't showing on my watch
features_wb_trouble_1: Open the watch's sync options in your settings and check that "Export workouts" is on.
features_wb_trouble_2: The session needs a structured workout. A session with only a duration has no steps to send.
features_wb_trouble_3: Sync the watch with its own app (Garmin Connect, Suunto, COROS). The workout sits there until the watch picks it up.
features_wb_trouble_4: On COROS, only running, trail and cycling are sent.
features_wb_trouble_5: Polar and Strava do not receive workouts at all.
features_wb_faq_1_q: Which watches receive my planned workouts?
features_wb_faq_1_a: Garmin, Suunto and COROS. Polar's API does not accept planned workouts and Strava has none, so both stay activity sources only.
features_wb_faq_2_q: Can I write targets as a percentage of VMA or FTP?
features_wb_faq_2_a: Yes: VMA, FTP, critical power, maximum heart rate and heart rate reserve. The watch gets an absolute pace, power or heart rate, computed from your latest value when the workout is sent.
features_wb_faq_3_q: What happens on the watch when I move a session?
features_wb_faq_3_a: The new version is sent for the new date. On COROS, which cannot delete planned workouts, the old slot keeps a "removed" placeholder.
features_wb_faq_4_q: Can my coach build the workouts for me?
features_wb_faq_4_a: Yes. Your coach builds them on your calendar or drops them from their library, and they go to your watch the same way as yours. You do not need a paid plan for that.
features_wb_faq_5_q: Is sending workouts to the watch free?
features_wb_faq_5_a: Yes, for everyone. On TrainingPeaks, getting planned workouts onto the watch is part of the Premium athlete plan (checked on 3 November 2026).
features_wb_final_body: Create an account, connect your Garmin, Suunto or COROS, and the next session you plan is on your wrist after the next sync.
tools_hub_seo_title: Free running calculators: pace, HR zones, race time
tools_hub_seo_description: Free calculators for runners and triathletes: maximum aerobic speed, heart rate zones, race time predictor, pace, trail time and grade-adjusted pace.
tools_hub_h1: Running calculators that show their maths
tools_hub_lead: Work out your paces, heart rate zones and race times in a few seconds. No account, no email, and every formula is written under the result.
tools_hub_next_title: Numbers are only useful once they are in your sessions.
tools_hub_next_body: In OpenAthlete, targets are written as a percentage of your VMA, threshold or max heart rate. Update the number once and every planned session follows, all the way to your Garmin, Suunto or COROS watch.
tools_hub_next_step1: Enter your VMA, zones or max heart rate in your profile
tools_hub_next_step2: Build “5 × 4' at 95% VMA” once, reuse it from the library
tools_hub_next_step3: The session lands on your watch with the right paces
tools_hub_final_title: Stop re-typing paces into your watch.
tools_hub_final_body: Plan structured sessions once, and OpenAthlete sends them to Garmin, Suunto and COROS. Free, open source.
tools_common_watch_title: Send these targets to your watch
tools_common_watch_body: Write your sessions in OpenAthlete with targets as a percentage of your VMA or max heart rate. They reach your Garmin, Suunto or COROS with the paces filled in.
tools_vma_seo_title: Maximum aerobic speed (VMA) calculator and paces
tools_vma_seo_description: Estimate your maximum aerobic speed (VMA) from a 6-minute test, a Cooper test or a race, and get your training paces for every zone.
tools_vma_lead: Your maximum aerobic speed (VMA, or vVO2max) is the speed you can hold for about six minutes flat out. Enter a test or a race result to get it, with the paces for every zone.
tools_vma_card: Your VMA from a field test or a race, and the paces that go with it.
tools_vma_z_marathon_use: Long runs with a race-pace finish
tools_vma_how_body: For the 6-minute and 12-minute tests, VMA is your average speed: distance divided by time. The 6-minute test is closest to the definition; over 12 minutes most runners slow down, so the Cooper result reads a little low. From a race, we divide your average speed by the share of VMA that distance is usually run at: about 95% for a 5K, 90% for a 10K, 85% for a half and 80% for a marathon. Treat race estimates as a starting point and retest every two or three months.
tools_vma_protocol_half: 6-minute test (demi-Cooper): after a 20-minute warm-up with a few strides, run as far as you can in 6 minutes on a track. Pace it evenly: starting too fast costs more than it gains.
tools_vma_protocol_cooper: Cooper test: the same, over 12 minutes. Easier to pace for beginners, but the result sits a little under your real VMA.
tools_vma_protocol_race: A race: use a recent, flat, all-out result. A 5K or 10K gives a better estimate than a marathon, where fuelling and heat weigh more.
tools_vma_faq1_a: It depends on age, sex and history. Many recreational runners sit between 12 and 16 km/h; well-trained club runners often reach 18 km/h and more. Compare yourself with your own last test, not with a table.
tools_vma_faq2_q: Is VMA the same as VO2max?
tools_vma_faq2_a: No. VO2max is the most oxygen your body can use, in ml/kg/min. VMA is the running speed at which you reach it. Two runners with the same VO2max can have different VMAs if one runs more economically.
tools_vma_faq3_a: Every 8 to 12 weeks, or at the start of each training block. Retest in similar conditions: same track, same time of day, rested legs.
tools_hr_seo_title: Karvonen Calculator: Heart Rate Zones from Resting HR
tools_hr_seo_description: Free Karvonen calculator: enter your resting and max heart rate and get your 5 training zones in bpm, zone 2 included, with the formula and an example.
tools_hr_lead: Five zones from your max and resting heart rate, with the Karvonen method or a simple percentage of max. Measured values beat formulas: enter them if you have them.
tools_hr_card: Five training zones from your max and resting heart rate.
tools_hr_max_hint: Leave empty to estimate it from your age: {value} bpm (Tanaka, 208 − 0.7 × age).
tools_hr_rest_hint: Taken in bed, just after waking up.
tools_hr_z2_use: Long runs and most easy days
tools_hr_how_body: The Karvonen formula works on your heart rate reserve, the gap between your max and resting heart rate: target heart rate = resting HR + (max HR − resting HR) × intensity. It gives higher, more personal numbers than a plain percentage of max, especially for fit runners with a low resting heart rate. The percentage method is simpler: each zone is a share of max, zone 2 being 60 to 70%.
tools_hr_faq1_q: How do I find my real max heart rate?
tools_hr_faq1_a: Look at the highest value your watch recorded at the end of a hard race or a hill repeat session, with a chest strap if you can. Wrist sensors often miss the peak.
tools_hr_faq2_a: Karvonen if you know your resting heart rate: it adapts to your fitness. The percentage of max is simpler and matches what many watches use by default.
tools_hr_faq3_q: Why does my heart rate drift up on long runs?
tools_hr_faq3_a: Heat, dehydration and fatigue raise heart rate at the same pace: that is cardiac drift. OpenAthlete measures it on each activity (aerobic decoupling) so you can see it improve over a block.
tools_rp_seo_title: Riegel Formula Calculator: Predict Your Race Times
tools_rp_seo_description: Riegel formula calculator: predict your 5K, 10K, half marathon and marathon times from a recent race, with goal paces, the 1.06 exponent and its source.
tools_rp_lead: Enter a recent race and see what it says about the others, with the pace to hold for each. A prediction assumes you trained for the distance, which matters most for the marathon.
tools_rp_card: From one race result to the others, with the pace for each.
tools_rp_how_body: The Riegel formula: T2 = T1 × (D2 / D1)^1.06, where T1 is your time over distance D1 and T2 the predicted time over D2. The exponent of 1.06 means you slow down a little each time the distance grows. It works best between similar distances and for runners who trained for the target. Beyond the half marathon, many runners land slower than predicted: long runs, fuelling and pacing are what close the gap.
tools_rp_faq1_q: Why is my marathon prediction too optimistic?
tools_rp_faq1_a: Riegel assumes marathon-specific training. Without regular long runs of 28 to 35 km, most runners lose 5 to 10 minutes on the prediction from a 10K.
tools_rp_faq2_a: A recent one (under three months), on a flat course, run all out. The closer it is to the target distance, the better the prediction.
tools_rp_faq3_q: Does it work for trail races?
tools_rp_faq3_a: No. Elevation, terrain and time on feet change everything. Use it for road races only.
tools_pace_seo_title: Pace calculator: min/km, km/h and race splits
tools_pace_seo_description: Convert a goal time into pace and speed (min/km, km/h) and get the splits for 5K, 10K, half marathon and marathon. Free running pace calculator.
tools_pace_lead: Type a distance and a goal time: get the pace per kilometre, the speed and the split at every checkpoint. Handy before a race, or to set a treadmill.
tools_pace_card: Goal time to pace, speed and splits.
tools_pace_how_body: Pace is time divided by distance, speed is distance divided by time: 5:00 per kilometre is 12 km/h. The splits assume an even pace. On a hilly course, or if you plan a negative split, run the first half a few seconds per kilometre slower than the average.
tools_pace_faq1_a: Running the second half faster than the first. Most road records are run that way: it saves glycogen early and keeps you passing people at the end.
tools_pace_faq2_q: Why does my watch show a different distance from the course?
tools_pace_faq2_a: Courses are measured on the shortest line, and GPS drifts between buildings and trees. Expect 200 to 500 m extra on a marathon, and aim for a pace a couple of seconds faster than the calculator says.
tools_pace_faq3_q: How do I set a treadmill from a pace?
tools_pace_faq3_a: Use the speed shown under the pace. Many runners add a 1% incline to make up for the missing air resistance.
athletes_seo_title: Free training app for runners and triathletes | OpenAthlete
athletes_seo_description: Plan your own training, send structured workouts to your watch, follow fitness, fatigue and form. Running, trail, cycling, triathlon. Every feature free.

athletes_watch_body: Activities arrive from Garmin, COROS, Suunto, Polar and Strava, or as FIT, GPX and TCX files. Planned workouts go to Garmin, COROS and Suunto watches. Switching brands next year? Your history stays where it is.

athletes_week_tue_body: The 5 × 4' at threshold you built with pace targets is already on your Garmin, COROS or Suunto. Run it, sync, and the activity links itself to the planned session.
athletes_week_thu_body: Laps graded against the plan, time in zones, aerobic decoupling, pace corrected for heat and slope. With AI turned on, a short read sums it up in three findings.
athletes_week_sun_title: Long run, then check your form
athletes_week_sun_body: Two hours on the trails. Fitness, fatigue and freshness update, and the curve runs on over next week's plan, so you already know whether Tuesday will hurt.
athletes_tools_title: What others sell as Premium, free here
athletes_tools_lead: No 14-day trial and no Premium tier for features. The free account is the whole app.
athletes_tools_season_body: Six or twelve months on one screen: blocks drawn with the mouse, A, B and C races, weekly load against the recommended range.
athletes_tools_builder_body: Warm-up, repeats, recoveries, targets in pace, heart rate, power or % of VMA and FTP. Save it once, drop it on any day.
athletes_tools_records_body: Best efforts from 400 m to 100 km, critical speed and power, race time ranges, Daniels training paces.
athletes_tools_analysis_body: Intervals and climbs detected for you, aerobic decoupling, grade-adjusted pace, weather along the route.
athletes_tools_periods_body: Mark the days off and OpenAthlete offers to move the planned sessions after the break, or clear them.
athletes_tools_metrics_body: Pulled from Garmin, COROS, Suunto or Polar and shown next to each day's freshness.
athletes_load_title: Real training load, with the maths in the open
athletes_load_body: Each activity gets a Banister TRIMP from your heart rate. Fitness is the 42-day average, fatigue the 7-day one, freshness the gap between them. Planned sessions get a load estimate too, so the curve runs ahead into next week.
athletes_load_open: The formulas sit in the source code, not behind a trademark. Read them, check them, argue about them on GitHub.
athletes_ai_title: Use the AI you already pay for
athletes_ai_body: Add a key from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral or another provider and every AI feature works on a free account. No key? Supporter includes a monthly allowance on ours. Nothing runs until you say yes.
athletes_ai_1_body: "Hilly 1h15 with 6 × 3' at 10K pace" becomes a structured workout built on your zones. You edit it like any other.
athletes_ai_2_body: How did it feel, how did you sleep, anything sore? Answer by text or by voice. Effort and pain go into your log.

athletes_faq_1_a: Yes. Calendar, workout builder, watch sync, analysis, records, training load and the MCP server are all on the free account, with no time limit. You only pay if you want AI on our keys instead of your own: Supporter, €5 a month or €50 a year.

athletes_faq_3_q: Will my past activities come with me?
athletes_faq_3_a: Connect Strava and your full history comes in; COROS sends it too, 50 files a day, so a long history takes a few days. Garmin and Suunto bring the last 30 days, and Polar only new activities. For the rest, upload FIT, GPX and TCX files in bulk.

athletes_faq_4_a: No. Most of the app is built for athletes who plan their own training. If you start working with a coach later, invite them and they plan in the same calendar.
athletes_faq_5_a: Yes. The Android app is on Google Play. The native iPhone app is in testing and coming soon; until then, the web app is designed for phones and installs on your home screen.
athletes_faq_6_q: What does the AI see, and can I turn it off?
athletes_faq_6_a: Only what each feature needs, sent to the provider of the key in use, and only after you allow it. You can withdraw that permission at any time in Settings, and turn off the post-activity questions on their own.
athletes_final_title: Your next block starts on Monday
athletes_final_body: Create an account and connect your watch. It takes two minutes, and your recent activities start coming in straight away.

opensource_host_title: Your own instance in three steps
opensource_host_lead: For a club, a lab, a coaching business, or just you.
opensource_host_1_body: Any Linux machine with Docker and its Compose plugin. 1 GB of RAM is enough: the stack uses about 250 MB at rest. Point your domain's DNS at it.
opensource_host_2_body: It downloads the Compose file, writes a .env with fresh secrets, pulls the images and starts PostgreSQL, Redis, the API, the web app and Caddy for automatic HTTPS.
opensource_host_3_body: Open your domain. The first account is yours; after that, sign-up is by invitation, so invite your athletes or coaches. Run the script again to update.

opensource_formulas_4: The AI prompts, word for word

compare_tp_seo_title: OpenAthlete vs TrainingPeaks: the free alternative compared
compare_tp_seo_description: Features, watch support, AI and price compared, now that Garmin owns TrainingPeaks. Open source and free, with workouts sent to Garmin, COROS and Suunto.
compare_tp_intro_1: TrainingPeaks has been the default for endurance coaching for years. Many coaches use it, many sell plans on its marketplace, and its Performance Management Chart taught a generation of athletes what CTL and TSB mean. It's a mature product, and it works.
compare_tp_intro_2: Two things changed the picture. Garmin bought it on July 22, 2026. And the bill grows with the roster: athletes need Premium for their workouts to reach the watch, and coaches pay per Premium athlete. OpenAthlete does the core of the job for free, with no per-athlete fee.
compare_tp_summary_them: You sell plans on a marketplace, ride on TrainingPeaks Virtual, or your athletes need store apps today.
compare_tp_summary_oa: You coach athletes on mixed watches, want workouts on the watch without Premium, and would rather not pay per athlete.
compare_tp_callout: Garmin bought TrainingPeaks on July 22, 2026. What that changes

compare_tp_better_oa_2_body: Five athletes free, then {oaYear} a year for the whole roster. No setup fee, no per-athlete line on the invoice. Thirty athletes all on Premium cost {tp30} a year on TrainingPeaks.

compare_tp_garmin_body_2: The question isn't whether your COROS keeps syncing next month. It's who decides, in five years, what an independent coaching platform is for.

compare_tp_faq_1_q: Is there a free alternative to TrainingPeaks?
compare_tp_faq_1_a: Yes. OpenAthlete is free on our servers with every feature: calendar, workout builder, workouts sent to Garmin, Suunto and COROS, training load, analysis, and coaching up to 5 athletes. Supporter ({oaMonth}/month or {oaYear}/year) adds AI on our keys and unlimited athletes. Self-hosting is free, with no limits.
compare_tp_faq_2_a: No. TSS is TrainingPeaks' metric. OpenAthlete computes load as Banister TRIMP from heart rate, or as session RPE (RPE × minutes) when there's no heart rate, then derives fitness (CTL, 42 days), fatigue (ATL, 7 days) and form (TSB). The formulas are in the source code.
compare_tp_faq_3_q: Will TrainingPeaks stop working with COROS, Suunto or Polar?
compare_tp_faq_3_a: Nobody outside Garmin knows, and we won't guess. The acquisition press release doesn't mention other brands. What we can say: OpenAthlete isn't owned by a watch maker, and its code is open, so no buyer can close it.
compare_tp_faq_4_q: Can I import my TrainingPeaks history?
compare_tp_faq_4_a: Your activities, yes. Strava and COROS bring your whole history, Garmin and Suunto the last 30 days, and you can upload older FIT, GPX and TCX files in bulk. Planned workouts and plans don't come across; rebuild your staple sessions as templates.
compare_tp_faq_5_q: Does OpenAthlete work for coaches with many athletes?
compare_tp_faq_5_a: Coaching is free up to 5 athletes and unlimited with Supporter at {oaYear} a year. You get a team overview with compliance and form, alerts for reported pain and inactivity, bulk move and copy on an athlete's calendar, and chat. There's no club account or marketplace yet.

compare_nolio_seo_description: Nolio and OpenAthlete compared for coaches and athletes: planning, watch sync, training load, AI and price. Free and open source, also from Grenoble.
compare_nolio_intro_1: Nolio is the platform French clubs know. It's a Grenoble company, a partner of the French athletics federation, and it says 4,500 coaches and 60,000 athletes use it. The free athlete tier is generous, the apps are native, and club pricing is built for associations.
compare_nolio_intro_2: We're from Grenoble too, so that's not the argument. The differences are elsewhere: the code is open and you can host it yourself, AI is built in with your own key, and above five athletes a coach pays {oaYear} a year, whatever the roster.
compare_nolio_summary_them: Your club needs association pricing with several coaches on one account, your athletes want store apps now, or you rely on the exercise videos.

compare_nolio_faq_2_q: Can I connect Claude or ChatGPT to my training?
compare_nolio_faq_2_a: Yes, through OpenAthlete's MCP server, on every plan. The assistant can read the calendar, activities, load and records, and plan up to 60 sessions at once. Changes show up in the calendar and reach Garmin, Suunto or COROS watches.
compare_nolio_faq_3_a: Yes, with limits. There's no club account: each coach has their own, and an athlete can have several coaches. One Supporter account can hold every athlete, or each coach above five athletes pays {oaYear} a year. A self-hosted instance has no limits at all.
compare_nolio_faq_4_a: Yes. The app speaks French, English, Spanish, Italian and Brazilian Portuguese.
compare_nolio_faq_5_a: From heart rate (Banister TRIMP) or session RPE, then fitness, fatigue and form, projected over the sessions you've planned. Every metric says what it measures and where it stops being reliable.
compare_icu_seo_title: OpenAthlete vs Intervals.icu: which free platform fits you?
compare_icu_seo_description: Two free training platforms compared: analysis depth, planning, coach tools, watch delivery, AI and MCP, open source and self-hosting.
compare_icu_intro_1: intervals.icu is one of the best things to happen to endurance data. It's free, it's fast, it reads almost every device on the market, and its analysis satisfies the most demanding power users. A {icuMonth} Supporter plan keeps it independent. Data-minded athletes love it, and they're right to.
compare_icu_intro_2: OpenAthlete takes a different angle. Less depth in the charts, more in the coaching loop: plan, send to the watch, ask the athlete how it went, act on it. The code is open, you can host it yourself, and AI is built in with your own key.
compare_icu_summary_them: You love power curves and custom charts, train on Wahoo or Zwift, or need an interface in one of 21 languages.
