races_seville_meta: Seville Marathon on 21 February 2027: pace for every goal, when to start a free 16-week plan, and how to race the flattest course in Europe.
races_seville_lead: Sunday 21 February 2027. The organisers call it the flattest marathon in Europe, ten metres between the lowest and highest point. Nothing to hide behind: it is you, the clock and a cold start.
races_seville_period: Sold out for 2027 (a record 20,000 entries); waiting list open.
races_seville_elevation: 10 m between the lowest and highest point, according to the organisers
races_seville_course: Flat city course on asphalt, crossing the Guadalquivir several times. In 2026: start on Avenida de María Luisa, finish on Paseo de las Delicias.
races_seville_weather: February: 7 to 18 °C on average (AEMET normals, Seville airport). Cold at the start, mild by the finish.
races_seville_hub: Ten metres of relief and a cold start: a pure pacing test.
races_seville_s1_b: No climbs also means no descents to relax on: the same muscles work for 42 km. The classic mistake here is the first 10 km 10 s/km too fast because it feels easy. Put 3 × 5 km at goal pace inside a 25 km long run, three or four times in the plan, and learn what goal pace feels like when you are fresh.
races_seville_s2_b: Counted back from 21 February, a 16-week plan started on Monday 2 November 2026. Starting now, skip the first weeks, never the last three. Christmas lands around week 8: keep that week easy and do the long run before the 24th.
races_seville_s3_b: February mornings in Seville often start in single digits. Wait in an old jumper you can leave at the start, wear cheap gloves for the first 10 km, and drink to schedule even if you are not thirsty: by the time slower runners finish, it is mild.
races_seville_faq1_a: Sunday 21 February 2027. Entries are sold out (a record 20,000) and a waiting list is open on the official site.
races_seville_faq2_q: Is Seville a good marathon for a personal best?
races_seville_faq2_a: On paper, one of the best: ten metres of relief according to the organisers and usually cool mornings. The course will not slow you down; going out too fast will. Pick the goal your recent half marathon supports and run even splits.
races_barcelona_h1: Barcelona Marathon 2027 training plan and pace guide
races_barcelona_meta: Barcelona Marathon on 14 March 2027: pace for every goal, the Monday to start a free 16-week plan, and the climbing the "flat" course hides.
races_barcelona_lead: Sunday 14 March 2027. The organisers sell it as flat and fast; GPS data says about 280 m of climbing. Fast, yes, if you run the drags by effort.
races_barcelona_cutoff: 6 hours after the last runner crosses the start; the race ends at 16:00
races_barcelona_course: Urban loop on asphalt: start on Passeig de Gràcia, the port and the seafront, then a long out-and-back on Avinguda Diagonal.
races_barcelona_weather: March: 10 to 16 °C on average (AEMET normals, Barcelona). Mild Mediterranean morning.
races_barcelona_hub: Sold as flat, climbs about 280 m: run the drags by effort.
races_barcelona_s1_t: "Flat and fast", with about 280 m of climbing
races_barcelona_s1_b: GPS data puts the gain near 280 m, much more than Seville or Valencia. It comes as long gentle drags, not hills. Do your goal-pace blocks on a route that rises and falls a little, and practise letting the pace drift 5 to 10 s/km on the way up while the effort stays the same.
races_barcelona_s2_b: A long straight avenue out, a turn, and the same avenue back: it is a head game more than a leg one. Run some long runs on one long straight road and split it into chunks: next kilometre, next drink, next 5 km marker.
races_barcelona_s3_b: Starts are staggered by the pace you declare. Overstate it and you spend 10 km being passed and pushed into a pace you cannot hold. Use the goal your training supports by February, not the one you typed in last summer.
races_barcelona_faq1_a: Sunday 14 March 2027, starting at 08:30. All 37,000 entries are sold. A 16-week plan starts on Monday 23 November 2026.
races_barcelona_faq2_q: Do I need a medical certificate for the Barcelona Marathon?
races_barcelona_faq2_a: No. The regulation asks for a health self-declaration, not a certificate. Runners must be 18 or older.
races_rome_h1: Rome Marathon 2027 training plan and pace guide
races_rome_meta: Rome Marathon on 14 March 2027: pace for every goal, the Monday to start a free 16-week plan, cobbles, and the medical certificate rule.
races_rome_lead: Sunday 14 March 2027, past the Colosseum, St Peter's and the Tiber. The profile is gentle; the sampietrini cobbles and the paperwork are what catch runners out.
races_rome_period: 32nd edition, held in any weather. 5 km fun run on Saturday 13 March.
races_rome_start: About 08:30 (regulation); in 2026 the waves left from 08:10 to 09:00
races_rome_course: Start on Via dei Fori Imperiali by the Colosseum, then the Tiber, Castel Sant'Angelo and Via della Conciliazione. Altitude between 8 and 31 m (organisers). Asphalt with cobbled sections.
races_rome_weather: March: 6 to 16 °C on average (NOAA normals, Rome Ciampino). Cool start, mild by midday.
races_rome_hub: Cobbles, tight turns and a medical certificate to sort out early.
races_rome_s1_b: Part of the course runs on Rome's cobbles (a press estimate puts it near a fifth). Test your race shoes on uneven ground before March: very soft, high plated shoes can feel unstable on cobbles and tight corners. Add calf raises and single-leg balance work twice a week, and run part of your easy runs on rough paths.
races_rome_s2_b: The historic centre means turns, narrow streets and short ramps up from the river. You will rarely hold one pace for long. In the last eight weeks, run your goal-pace blocks on a twisting city loop rather than a straight towpath, and get used to settling back to pace after every corner without sprinting out of it.
races_rome_s3_b: Runners living outside Italy need a RUNCARD and a medical certificate for competitive athletics, to Italian standards, uploaded when they register. Minimum age is 20. Book the medical early: it often needs an exercise ECG, and you do not want to chase it in week 14.
races_rome_faq1_a: Sunday 14 March 2027, the 32nd edition, with a start around 08:30 and a 7-hour limit. Registration is open on the official site. A 16-week plan starts on Monday 23 November 2026.
races_rome_faq2_q: Do foreign runners need a medical certificate for the Rome Marathon?
races_rome_faq2_a: Yes. The 2027 regulation asks non-Italian residents for a RUNCARD plus a medical certificate for competitive athletics, to Italian standards, uploaded at registration. Check the exact wording in the regulation linked above.
races_milan_h1: Milan Marathon 2027 training plan and pace guide
races_milan_meta: Milan Marathon on 4 April 2027: pace for every goal, the Monday to start a free 16-week plan, and how to pace a flat point-to-point course.
races_milan_lead: Sunday 4 April 2027, the 25th edition. In 2026 the course ran point to point from Corso Sempione to the Duomo, with about 45 m of climbing by GPS. Flat enough for a PB, as long as April stays cool.
races_milan_period: 25th edition. Registration open on the official site.
races_milan_start: Not published for 2027 (waves at 08:15, 08:30 and 08:45 in 2026, press)
races_milan_cutoff: 6h30 according to third-party listings; check the 2027 regulation
races_milan_course: 2026: point to point from Corso Sempione to Piazza del Duomo, on asphalt with some city-centre paving. The 2027 route is not published yet.
races_milan_weather: April: 8 to 19 °C on average (normals for Milan Linate). Cool start, can be warm by late morning.
races_milan_hub: Flat, point to point, finishing at the Duomo. Watch the late-morning sun.
races_milan_s1_b: A point-to-point course with about 45 m of climbing (GPS data) is made for even splits. Your job is to know goal pace in your legs. From week 8, put 2 to 3 blocks of 4 to 6 km at goal pace into the Sunday long run, and check your halfway split on the pace chart.
races_milan_s2_b: April averages top out near 19 °C, and a 4h30 runner finishes around midday. Drink at the early aid stations, not only when it gets hot, and practise it: take a drink every 5 km in your last four long runs, from a cup if you can.
races_milan_s3_t: A block that starts in December
races_milan_s3_b: A 16-week plan starts on Monday 14 December 2026: the holidays fall in weeks 2 and 3, the hard work in February and March. If a winter illness costs you a week, skip it rather than squeezing two weeks into one.
races_milan_faq1_a: Sunday 4 April 2027, the 25th edition, the same day as the Paris Marathon. Registration is open. The start times and the 2027 route are not published yet.
races_milan_faq2_a: Yes. GPS data gives about 45 m of climbing for the recent course, and since 2026 it runs point to point with no repeated laps. The organisers do not publish an elevation figure, and the 2027 route is still to come.
races_london_h1: London Marathon 2027 training plan and pace guide
races_london_meta: London Marathon 2027 runs over two days, 24 and 25 April: pace for every goal, the Monday to start a free 16-week plan, and the GPS trap.
races_london_lead: For 2027 only, London runs over two days: women on Saturday 24 April, men on Sunday 25 April. Same point-to-point course from Greenwich to The Mall, same two traps: a downhill start and GPS that goes mad in Canary Wharf.
races_london_period: One-off two-day event: women race on Saturday, men on Sunday.
races_london_start: Not published for 2027 (mass waves from about 09:30 to 11:30 in 2026, press)
races_london_cutoff: Saturday: finish on The Mall closes at 17:30. Sunday: a second finish stays open until 23:59.
races_london_course: Point to point on asphalt: three starts in Greenwich and Blackheath merge before mile 3, then Cutty Sark, Tower Bridge before halfway, Canary Wharf, and the finish on The Mall.
races_london_weather: Late April: 6 to 15 °C on average (Met Office normals, Greenwich Park). Warm years happen.
races_london_hub: Two days in 2027, a downhill start and GPS chaos in Canary Wharf.
races_london_s1_t: Do not bank time in the first 3 miles
races_london_s1_b: The first three miles are net downhill and get crowded where the three starts merge. Running them 15 s/km fast feels free and costs you after mile 20. Finish every long run with the opposite habit: the first 5 km 5 to 10 s/km slower than goal pace, then settle.
races_london_s2_b: Between miles 15 and 20, tall buildings throw GPS pace off; the organisers advise using the mile markers. Learn your goal pace per mile (the pace chart gives it) and set your watch to show lap time against manual laps, or just elapsed time to compare with a pace band.
races_london_s3_b: Women race on Saturday, men on Sunday, so the plan start is the same: Monday 4 January 2027. If you race on Saturday, move the long run to Saturday for the last eight weeks, and rehearse race breakfast at the race start time.
races_london_faq1_a: Over two days, as a one-off: Saturday 24 April 2027 for the women (elite, para-athletes, championship and Good For Age) and Sunday 25 April 2027 for the men. Ballot entrants were entered for both days.
races_london_faq2_q: How do you get a place in the London Marathon?
races_london_faq2_a: Three ways: the random ballot (the 2027 ballot ran from 24 April to 1 May 2026), Good For Age places for UK residents (a qualifying time does not guarantee one), and charity places.
races_berlin_h1: Berlin Marathon 2027 training plan and pace guide
races_berlin_meta: Berlin Marathon on 26 September 2027: pace for every goal, the Monday to start a free 16-week plan, and how to train through the summer.
races_berlin_lead: Sunday 26 September 2027 on the course of the world records: wide, flat streets and a finish through the Brandenburg Gate. The hard part is the build, sixteen weeks of summer.
races_berlin_period: Entry by lottery, open on the official site.
races_berlin_cutoff: 6h15 from crossing the start line (registration terms)
races_berlin_course: Loop on wide, flat streets from Straße des 17. Juni, finishing behind the Brandenburg Gate. The organisers call it the flattest of the World Marathon Majors.
races_berlin_weather: Late September: 10 to 20 °C on average (DWD normals, Berlin). Some years are warm.
races_berlin_hub: The world-record course. The catch: a summer-long build.
races_berlin_s1_b: Eliud Kipchoge ran 2:01:09 here in 2022. For the rest of us, the lesson is the same: flat, wide roads reward the runner who holds one pace. Rehearse it with a 30 km run at the end of the plan, the last 12 km at goal pace, and check the halfway split on the pace chart.
races_berlin_s2_b: A 16-week plan starts on Monday 7 June 2027, so most of the work happens in July and August. Run the long runs early in the morning, accept easy paces 10 to 20 s/km slower on hot days, and judge the quality sessions by effort or heart rate. September will feel easy by comparison.
races_berlin_s3_b: The organisers list 15 aid stations, with gels at 27.5 km, and runners can hand in their own drinks for 5, 9, 15, 20, 25, 30, 36 and 40 km. Whatever you choose, practise it: in your last five long runs, drink and take a gel on that exact schedule.
races_berlin_faq1_a: Sunday 26 September 2027. Start times are not published yet. A 16-week plan starts on Monday 7 June 2027.
races_berlin_faq2_q: How do you get into the Berlin Marathon?
races_berlin_faq2_a: Through a lottery, open on the official site for 2027. Entry conditions and dates are on the official site.
races_valencia_h1: Valencia Marathon 2027 training plan and pace guide
races_valencia_meta: Valencia Marathon 2027: date not out yet, usually the first Sunday of December. Pace for every goal, when to start a free 16-week plan.
races_valencia_lead: The 2026 edition runs on Sunday 6 December and is sold out; it is too close to start a plan now. For 2027, expect the first Sunday of December again, on one of the fastest courses in the world.
races_valencia_period: Usually the first Sunday of December. The 2026 edition is on Sunday 6 December 2026 and is sold out.
races_valencia_cutoff: About 5h30 according to secondary sources; not confirmed in the official regulation
races_valencia_course: Flat, at sea level, on asphalt. Start on Plaça de la Marató, finish on the walkway over the water at the City of Arts and Sciences.
races_valencia_weather: December: 8 to 17 °C on average (AEMET normals, Valencia). Often dry and cool.
races_valencia_hub: Flat, cool, at sea level: the PB course. 2027 date to come.
races_valencia_s1_t: A course that will not slow you down
races_valencia_s1_b: About 47 m of climbing by GPS, sea level and a December morning: the men's course record is 2:01:48 (Sisay Lemma, 2023). If a PB is the goal, train its pace with precision. Long runs with 2 × 8 km at goal pace in the last six weeks, on flat ground, and nothing faster than planned.
races_valencia_s2_t: A build that starts in August
races_valencia_s2_b: Counted back from the first Sunday of December, a 16-week plan starts in the second half of August, so the first month is hot. Keep it easy, run early, and save the fast work for September and October. Once the 2027 date is official, this page will show the exact Monday.
races_valencia_s3_t: A huge field: seed yourself honestly
races_valencia_s3_b: Expect the first 5 km to be crowded. Starting in a box faster than your real level only means being passed and pushed. Lose 20 seconds in the first kilometres rather than two minutes after km 35.
races_valencia_faq1_a: Not announced yet (checked on 4 November 2026). The race is usually held on the first Sunday of December: 7 December in 2025, 6 December in 2026. Wait for the official date before booking travel.
races_valencia_faq2_q: I am running Valencia on 6 December 2026. Is it too late for a plan?
races_valencia_faq2_a: For a full 16-week plan, yes. With about four weeks left, open one of our marathon plans and follow its last four weeks: one more long run with goal-pace blocks, then a two-week taper. Fitness is built now; the aim is to arrive fresh.
races_rio_h1: Rio Marathon 2027 training plan and pace guide
races_rio_meta: Rio Marathon on 30 May 2027: pace for every goal, the Monday to start a free 16-week plan, and how to prepare for heat, humidity and a dawn start.
races_rio_lead: Sunday 30 May 2027, late May this time, not June. Expect around 21 °C at dawn and 80% humidity on an exposed seafront: the pace you pick matters more than the pace you can hold in a cool city.
races_rio_period: 25th edition, 27–30 May 2027 (half marathon on Saturday 29). The 42K is sold out.
races_rio_elevation: 2027 course not published. The 2026 course: 110 m of climbing (organisers).
races_rio_course: 2026: point to point along the coast, from Praia da Reserva (Barra da Tijuca) to Marina da Glória, Aterro do Flamengo, on asphalt. The 2027 course is not published yet.
races_rio_weather: Late May: 21 to 28 °C on average, about 80% humidity (INMET normals, Rio de Janeiro).
races_rio_hub: Late May, dawn start, 80% humidity: pick a goal for the heat.
races_rio_s1_t: Heat and humidity from the gun
races_rio_s1_b: Even at dawn it is around 21 °C with 80% humidity, and sweat barely cools you. If you live somewhere cooler, give yourself 10 to 14 days of heat exposure before the race (easy runs in the warm part of the day, or sauna after training), and practise drinking with salt from week 6.
races_rio_s2_b: The 2026 start was at 05:30 on a point-to-point course, so you are up around 03:00 and on transport well before 05:00. Rehearse it twice: an alarm at 03:00, your race breakfast, and a long run at the race start time.
races_rio_s3_t: Pick a goal for the conditions
races_rio_s3_b: Heat costs time, and it costs more the longer you are out. A fair rule: take the goal your training supports for a cool race and pick the next slower line in the table. A 3h45 runner in Berlin is a 4h00 runner in Rio, and still has a great day.
races_rio_faq1_a: The marathon is on Sunday 30 May 2027, during the 25th edition (27 to 30 May, with the half on Saturday 29 May). The 42K is sold out; the regulation sets a minimum age of 20.
races_rio_faq2_q: Is the Rio Marathon in June?
races_rio_faq2_a: Not in 2027. The 2026 edition was on 6 and 7 June, but the 2027 regulation puts the marathon on 30 May, on the Corpus Christi long weekend. Count your 16 weeks back from that date: the plan starts on Monday 8 February 2027.
races_saintelyon_h1: SaintéLyon 2026 training guide: night, cold and 2,500 m of climbing
races_saintelyon_meta: SaintéLyon on 28–29 November 2026: 80 km and 2,500 m at night from Saint-Étienne to Lyon. The last three weeks, and how to build for 2027.
races_saintelyon_lead: Saturday night, 23:30, Saint-Étienne: 80 km over the Monts du Lyonnais to Lyon, mostly in the dark, in late November. The 2026 edition is three weeks away; this page covers the last stretch and the build for next year.
races_saintelyon_period: 72nd edition; the 80 km solo is full. The 2027 date is not announced yet.
races_saintelyon_start: 23:30 on Saturday, from the Parc des Expositions in Saint-Étienne
races_saintelyon_cutoff: Finish in Lyon closes at 16:00 on Sunday; first barrier at km 17 at 04:00
races_saintelyon_course: Night point to point from Saint-Étienne to the Halle Tony Garnier in Lyon, over the crests of the Monts du Lyonnais: trails, forest tracks and tarmac lanes. About 40% of the course is new in 2026. Five aid stations.
races_saintelyon_weather: Late November: 5 to 11 °C on average in Lyon (Météo-France normals, Lyon-Bron), colder on the night crests. Past editions saw frost, snow, ice and mud.
races_saintelyon_hub: A whole night from Saint-Étienne to Lyon, ice optional. In three weeks.
races_saintelyon_s1_t: A whole night on your feet
races_saintelyon_s1_b: You start at 23:30 after a full day awake, and most runners finish after sunrise. Train it: three or four night runs with your race headlamp, one of them starting late after a normal day. On race day, sleep in late, nap in the afternoon, and eat your usual dinner early.
races_saintelyon_s2_b: The main hazard in some editions has been ice on the tarmac lanes, in others slippery mud. Run your downhills on both road and muddy trail, short steps and eyes three metres ahead, and pick shoes for grip over cushioning. A fall at km 60 costs more than any minute saved.
races_saintelyon_s3_t: Racing on 28 November? Three weeks to go
races_saintelyon_s3_b: No fitness is gained now. One last long outing this weekend (around 3 hours with climbing), then cut volume by a third, then by half in race week. Test the headlamp, spare battery and layers on a night run, and sleep. For 2027, build from the summer with our 50 km plan as the base block.
races_saintelyon_faq1_a: The night of Saturday 28 to Sunday 29 November 2026, start at 23:30 in Saint-Étienne for the 80 km and the relays. The 2027 date is not announced yet.
races_saintelyon_faq2_a: The 80 km solo, relays for teams of 2, 3 or 4, the LyonSaintéLyon (160 km, Lyon to Saint-Étienne and back), the SaintExpress (46 km), the SaintéVia (36 km), the SaintéSprint (25 km) and the SaintéTic (13 km).
races_utmb_h1: UTMB 2027 training guide: course, kit and preparation
races_utmb_meta: UTMB 2027: 174 km and 9,700 m around Mont Blanc, dates not announced yet. How to train for the climbing, the nights and the mandatory kit.
races_utmb_lead: A loop of the Mont-Blanc massif through France, Italy and Switzerland: 174 km and 9,700 m of climbing in 2026, with 45h30 to finish. Most of it is hiked, much of it at night, and the weather can go from 30 °C to snow.
races_utmb_period: Usually the last week of August (24–30 August in 2026). The press reports the week may move in 2027 because of the road cycling World Championships in Haute-Savoie.
races_utmb_course: A loop around the Mont-Blanc massif from and to Chamonix, through France, Italy and Switzerland: mountain trails, cols above 2,000 m, technical descents. Shorter races of the week: CCC (108 km, 6,200 m) and OCC (60 km, 3,500 m).
races_utmb_weather: August in Chamonix: 9 to 23 °C on average (Météo-France normals). The organisers warn of 30 °C in the valleys and down to −10 °C felt above 2,000 m, with rain, hail or snow.
races_utmb_hub: 174 km, 9,700 m, two nights for most. 2027 dates to come.
races_utmb_s1_b: The climbs are long, and almost everyone hikes them. Your uphill walking speed decides your finish time more than your flat pace. From six months out, one session a week of 30 to 60 min steep hiking with poles, and long days in the mountains where you climb 2,000 m or more.
races_utmb_s2_t: One night for sure, two for most
races_utmb_s2_b: With an evening start, everyone runs the first night and most finishers see a second one. Plan where you would take a 10 to 20 minute nap if you need it, and try a short nap once in training, on a long night outing, to know how you wake up from it.
races_utmb_s3_t: Train with the full mandatory kit
races_utmb_s3_b: The organisers publish a mandatory equipment list and can add a cold-weather kit when the forecast demands it. Carry the full pack, cold kit included, on every long day from May, so the weight and the fit are no surprise in August.
races_utmb_faq1_q: How do you get into UTMB?
races_utmb_faq1_a: Through a lottery weighted by Running Stones, earned at UTMB World Series events (at least one within the two years before the lottery), plus a valid UTMB Index in the 100K or 100M category. Pre-registration is usually in December and the lottery in January. Rules can change: check the official site.
races_utmb_faq2_a: The dates were not announced on 4 November 2026. The race usually takes place in the last week of August, but the press reports it may have to move in 2027 because of the road cycling World Championships in Haute-Savoie (24 August to 5 September 2027).
races_diagonale_h1: Diagonale des Fous 2027 training guide: qualifying, terrain, kit
races_diagonale_meta: Diagonale des Fous 2027 on Réunion: 180 km and 10,200 m, dates not out yet. Qualifying races, technical terrain, heat and cold, and how to train.
races_diagonale_lead: Across Réunion from Saint-Pierre to Saint-Denis: 180 km and 10,200 m of climbing in 2026, through the cirques of the National Park, with 66 hours to finish. You have to qualify first, and the terrain is slower than anything in the Alps.
races_diagonale_period: Every October, mid-month (15–18 October in 2026). The 2027 dates are not announced yet.
races_diagonale_start: Thursday 22:00 from Saint-Pierre in 2026, at night
races_diagonale_course: Point to point across the island, from Saint-Pierre to the Stade de La Redoute in Saint-Denis, through the cirques of the Réunion National Park: very technical volcanic trails, steps, rocks and roots. The route can change.
races_diagonale_weather: October on the coast: 20 to 27 °C on average (Météo-France normals, Saint-Denis). Cooler and changeable at altitude, especially at night.
races_diagonale_hub: 180 km of volcanic steps, roots and rock. Qualify first.
races_diagonale_s1_t: Slower per km than the Alps
races_diagonale_s1_b: Steps, roots and wet volcanic rock make the time per km far slower than in the Alps for the same climbing. Train on the worst ground you have: stairs, rocky paths, steep forest. Add step-ups and step-downs with a loaded pack twice a week, and forget pace: judge long days by hours and climbing.
races_diagonale_s2_b: The coast is tropical, the high ground is cool and changeable, and the start is at night. Train with the full kit in your pack, test your rain layer in real rain, and do a few long runs in the heat of the day if you come from a cooler climate.
races_diagonale_s3_b: The regulation asks for two finished races of at least 85 km-effort points each (1 km = 1 point, 100 m of climbing = 1 point) within a set period. Put them in your season on purpose: they are your longest training days, so space them at least two months apart and recover from each.
races_diagonale_faq1_q: How do you qualify for the Diagonale des Fous?
races_diagonale_faq1_a: The regulation asks for two finished single-stage foot races of at least 85 km-effort points each (1 km = 1 point, 100 m of climbing = 1 point) within a set period, plus a medical certificate or licence. In 2026 the entry fee was €260 and the field was capped at 3,000 runners.
races_diagonale_faq2_q: When is the 2027 Diagonale des Fous?
races_diagonale_faq2_a: Not announced on 4 November 2026. The Grand Raid is held every October, around the middle of the month: in 2026 it ran from 15 to 18 October, with the Diagonale starting on Thursday at 22:00.
